lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: symmetry and rule-based patterns in the completed design
lessonRef.title: Transfer, reflection, and publication: symmetry and rule-based patterns in the completed design

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different setting than the problems below.

items.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?

steps: A square matches itself when folded along 2 diagonals and 2 midlines.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: The pattern 2, 4, 8, 16, ... follows the rule "multiply by 2 each time." What is the 6th term?
How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
The pattern 1, 2, 4, 8, ... follows the rule "multiply by 2 each time." What is the 5th term?
How many lines of symmetry does a equilateral triangle have?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: The pattern 6, 18, 54, 162, ... follows the rule "multiply by 3 each time." What is the 6th term?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
